title: Make, freeze, test, and defend a change
notes: CORE · 2 min explanation. Teaching purpose: Actually change the feature code; preserve the baseline and defend the result. Mechanism and worked reasoning: Experiment C accepts a useful improvement or an honest negative result. A new seed, copied answer or fluent AI narrative alone is not a changed modeling assumption. Ask: What is the minimum student action? Expected explanation: Edit an X-only feature function, predict its effect, keep the declared controls, execute the comparison and explain the observed outcome. This is class practice, not a new graded Homework. Visual interpretation: Instructional protocol: highlighted dependency 1. No empirical performance claim. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again. title: A feature change is a modeling hypothesis
notes: CORE · 2 min explanation. Teaching purpose: The feature function receives inputs only and preserves original column order. Mechanism and worked reasoning: Append a deterministic input transformation. Do not pass labels, split IDs or row identifiers into the feature function. Test shape, finiteness, deterministic output and no in-place mutation before fitting. Ask: Why does the starting identity remain a draft? Expected explanation: It has not changed the model basis. The notebook can run for orientation, but presence of text or successful execution does not establish an implemented or correct experiment. Visual interpretation: Input-only feature functions; no labels or row IDs. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again. title: Freeze the plan before a new audit
notes: CORE · 2 min explanation. Teaching purpose: Record code, hypothesis, expected outcome and held-fixed conditions. Mechanism and worked reasoning: Fit on original train, inspect validation, then save source and plan identity before materializing the new independent synthetic audit sample. This is a learning contract, not an adversarial security barrier. Ask: Can the same audit be reused to tune repeatedly? Expected explanation: That turns it into development data. Disclose the reuse as exploratory and seek a new evaluation for a confirmatory claim. A hash records bytes, not honesty or correctness. Visual interpretation: Instructional protocol: highlighted dependency 1. No empirical performance claim. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. title: Compare paired outcomes with a preserved baseline
notes: CORE · 2 min explanation. Teaching purpose: Use the same audit rows and metric for both models. Mechanism and worked reasoning: Plot both prediction vectors and report baseline and student MAE on 240 fresh audit rows. Keep the original selected model; do not silently replace it or reselect from audit outcomes. Ask: Does beating the baseline prove a general result? Expected explanation: No. It is evidence for this code, sample and declared comparison. Discuss sampling variation, synthetic assumptions and whether the same conclusion should hold in another problem. Visual interpretation: Actual new audit vectors, same 240 rows. Worked square and independent cubic code fixtures are clearly distinguished. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again. [Sources] https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/ensemble/plot_bias_variance.html; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html; https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/production-ml-systems/monitoring

title: A negative result can still be explanatory
notes: REFERENCE · use during practice / no extra lecture time. Teaching purpose: A changed feature is not automatically a useful feature. Mechanism and worked reasoning: An added odd-power feature may fail to represent an even square under symmetric inputs. Inspect the outcome instead of forcing an improvement claim. A valid edit can produce a valid unsuccessful experiment. Ask: What should students defend when MAE rises? Expected explanation: The original hypothesis, the exact change, held-fixed conditions, measured outcome and a plausible mechanism with limitations. Honest evidence and independent reasoning matter more than a favorable score. Visual interpretation: Analytic feature geometry on synthetic input points; not a performance result. Facilitation: get a prediction first, inspect matching notebook outputs, and distinguish finite empirical observations from population formulas. Live laboratory blocks include discussion and navigation through reference pages; do not time every page again.
